ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left of the figure is a benzene ring, and an oxygen atom is connected to the benzene ring; this oxygen atom is then connected to AlCl3, and there are three chlorines around aluminum. On the right is shown an oxygen-positive carbonyl/acyl fragment, and the carbonyl carbon is connected to R. The figure also has curved arrows, but the question requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning count: Count by fragments and do not count hydrogen-related bonds: inside the benzene ring there are 6 C–C bonds; there is 1 bond from the aryl carbon to oxygen; there is 1 bond from oxygen to aluminum; there are 3 Al–Cl bonds from aluminum to the three chlorines; the right-side carbonyl C=O is counted as 1 bond; there is 1 bond from the carbonyl carbon to R. The total is 6 + 1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 13.

raw_record.question_text: In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen. Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First describe the visible structure. Count by fragments: benzene ring has 6 C–C ring bonds; the aryl carbon to oxygen bond adds 1; the oxygen to aluminum bond adds 1; aluminum to its three chlorines adds 3; the right-hand carbonyl C=O counts as 1 bond; the carbonyl carbon to R counts as 1 bond. Add all components: 6+1+1+3+1+1 = 13.
